preamble: Comments aren't in your document the way words are. They're a separate layer, pinned to bits of text, and Docs decides how much of that layer to draw on screen. So when you can't see comments, nothing is missing — the layer is just turned down. What you're about to change isn't the document at all; it's your view of it.
generalization: Anything that changes what you can see without changing what's in the file lives under View. Rulers, outlines, comments — none of those are content, they're how the content is drawn for you. If a change would look different to your collaborator than to you, look in View first.

steps.intent: Comments belong to the document no matter what you do here — the only question is whether they're drawn on your screen. That kind of question, what's shown rather than what exists, has its own menu.
hints: You're not adding anything or editing anything. You're changing what gets displayed to you and only you.
The menu bar at the top, third from the left, between Edit and Insert.

wrongHints.Insert: Insert is how you make a new comment. Reasonable guess — but the comments already exist; you want to look at them, not create one.
wrongHints.Edit: Edit changes the document's contents. Whether comments are visible on your screen doesn't change the document for anyone else.

steps.intent: Docs doesn't offer a single on/off switch for comments — it offers degrees of visibility, so it gathers them into their own group. Open that group.
hints: There's more than one way to show a comment, so the options are nested rather than sitting loose in the menu.
In the View menu that just opened, with a small arrow on the right meaning a submenu follows.

wrongHints.Mode: Mode decides whether you're editing, suggesting or viewing. It affects what you can do to the document, not what you can see alongside it.

steps.intent: Your turn. Of the options here, one turns the layer fully up: every comment on the page, open and readable, rather than tucked away. Pick that one.
hints: Two of these make comments smaller or take them away. You want the opposite direction.
The option in this submenu that promises all of them, not some of them.
